newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Sen. Faircloth calls D.C. plan 'rip off'.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Sen. Faircloth calls D.C. plan 'rip off'.

text.p: President Clinton's plan to rescue District of Columbia is a "rip off," the chairman of the Senate Appropriations subcommittee on D.C. said Tuesday.

"From the few details I have seen, I like a greater federal role in District affairs. However, this plan could be called the 'great rip off,' not the 'great swap'," Sen. Lauch Faircloth, R-N.C., said in a statement.
The White House announced a $3.9 billion five-year federal aid plan for the district and said it was ending the $3.56 billion federal payment to the city over that period.

"Any plan that increases the federal deficit is a non-starter with me," Faircloth said. "How can we plausibly discuss cutting Medicare and the cost of living adjustment for Social Security recipients, and at the same time provide a multi-billion dollar bail-out for a mismanaged city?"
Faircloth also said he was "suspicious" of any plan that spends money now for future savings.
"What assurances do we have that fundamental changes will be made, but local leaders, not just the Control Board, so that there will never be another bail-out of D.C. again?" Faircloth said.
Rep. Thomas Davis, R-Va., chairman of the House Government Reform subcommittee on D.C., was in China but had been briefed on Clinton's proposal, spokesman John Hishta said.
"Obviously there are a lot of details to be worked out and we'll be holding a lot of hearings this spring on the matter," Hishta said.
